title: Identify from a photo
subtitle: Narrow down what you're looking at

disclaimer.beforeCapture: This tool narrows down possible species from a photo. It never confirms that something is safe to eat.
disclaimer.aboveResults: These are possible matches, not a confirmed identification. A dangerous look-alike can be correct even when it is not the top result.
disclaimer.neverEat: Do not eat anything based on this app. Check the distinguishing features below against a field guide, and ask someone experienced if there is any doubt.

results.heading: Possible matches
results.toxicBanner: One of these matches is toxic. Read every row before going further.
results.notInCatalog: Not in this app's catalog — no safety information

mechanisms.amatoxin: Contains amatoxins — the same toxin group as the death cap. Poisoning is often delayed by 6–24 hours, feels like recovery, then causes liver failure. Frequently fatal.
mechanisms.gyromitrin: Contains gyromitrin, which the body converts to a toxin damaging the liver and nervous system. Can be fatal, and is not reliably destroyed by cooking.
mechanisms.muscarine: Contains high levels of muscarine, causing rapid sweating, salivation and collapse. Deaths have been recorded.
mechanisms.orellanine: Contains orellanine, which destroys the kidneys. Symptoms can take days to weeks to appear, long after the meal is forgotten.
mechanisms.isoxazole: Contains ibotenic acid and muscimol, causing confusion, nausea and delirium. Rarely fatal but seriously unpleasant.
mechanisms.giIrritant: Causes severe vomiting and diarrhoea, sometimes for days. Not usually fatal, but dehydration can be dangerous.
mechanisms.colchicine: Contains colchicine. There is no antidote, symptoms are delayed, and a small amount can kill an adult.
mechanisms.cardiacGlycoside: Contains cardiac glycosides that disturb the heart rhythm. Can be fatal.
mechanisms.calciumOxalate: Contains needle-like calcium oxalate crystals that burn and swell the mouth and throat.
mechanisms.coniine: Contains coniine, the poison in hemlock. It paralyses the muscles used for breathing. Very small amounts are fatal.
mechanisms.tropane: Contains tropane alkaloids. A handful of berries can kill a child. Sweet taste offers no warning.
mechanisms.poorEdibility: Not dangerous, but poor eating and easily mistaken for something better.
mechanisms.bitter: Not poisonous, but so bitter that a single specimen ruins a whole dish.

checks.volva: Look at the very base of the stem, below ground level: a sac-like bag or swollen cup there is a serious warning sign.
checks.gillColour: Gill colour, including on older specimens — pure white gills on a stemmed mushroom deserve caution.
checks.gillAttachment: Whether the underside has true blade-like gills that can be separated with a fingernail.
checks.gillVsRidges: True chanterelles have blunt, forking ridges running down the stem, not thin crowded gills.
checks.sporePrint: Take a spore print: leave the cap gill-side down on paper for a few hours and check the colour.
checks.ringAndStem: Whether there is a ring on the stem, whether it slides freely, and any pattern on the stem below it.
checks.overallSize: Full-grown size. Some deadly look-alikes are much smaller than the edible species they resemble.
checks.capWarts: Whether the cap has removable patches or warts, which can wash off in rain.
checks.cortina: Any cobweb-like veil between cap edge and stem on young specimens, and rusty-brown traces where it was.
checks.capStructure: Whether the head is a regular pitted honeycomb or an irregular brain-like set of folds.
checks.capAttachment: Whether the cap is attached to the stem along its length or hangs free from the top only.
checks.hollowStem: Cut the specimen in half lengthways and check whether it is completely hollow inside.
checks.poreColour: Colour of the pores under the cap, especially any red or orange tones.
checks.fleshBruising: Whether cut or bruised flesh changes colour, and to what.
checks.fleshReddening: Whether the flesh reddens where handled or damaged.
checks.stemNetwork: Any raised net-like pattern on the stem, and its colour.
checks.smell: Crush a leaf or piece and smell it. Wild garlic smells strongly of garlic; its deadly look-alikes do not.
checks.leafArrangement: How leaves emerge: singly from the base on their own stalk, or paired and sheathed together.
checks.leafShape: Leaf outline and veining, including whether the base is arrow-shaped.
checks.stemMarkings: Whether the stem is hollow, ridged, or blotched with purple — and whether it smells unpleasant when crushed.
checks.berryArrangement: Whether berry clusters droop below the branches or stand upright above the foliage.
checks.plantHabit: Whether the plant is a woody shrub or a soft green herb dying back each year.

critical.lepiotaMacrolepiota: Deadly Lepiota species are among the most dangerous look-alikes for the Parasol mushroom, and this was the single most frequent mistake in our testing. A true Parasol is large, with a movable ring and a snakeskin-patterned stem. Small specimens with a plain stem should be left alone even if they look right.
